headline: Models reuse knowledge across cohorts and cancers, with scrutiny of baselines and calibration
label: Transfer And Validation In Cancer
summary: Preprints pair cross-cohort and cross-cancer transfer with tests against simple baselines, showing where added model complexity does or does not help.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reuse of learned structure across cohorts, cancer types, or data layers, paired with evaluation of what that reuse delivers. A layer-specific transfer elastic net borrows from older breast cancer cohorts to improve survival prediction in patients under 50, and an axillary lymph node deep-learning model is assessed for cross-cancer metastasis prediction. Other items bear on generalisation more than transfer. The multimodal ER/PR/HER2 model has strong cross-cohort AUCs but poor calibration and no gain over a 3-gene baseline. In TCGA classification, logistic regression is strongest among five learners and three ensembles. CAISL anchors LUAD survival models to clinical variables with sparse molecular correction. Calibration and simple-baseline comparison are the sharper points.
